newsitem.title: USA: New York Gov. Pataki boosted in poll.
newsitem.headline: New York Gov. Pataki boosted in poll.

text.p: Republican Gov. George Pataki, who won election in 1994 on promises to restore the death penalty and cut taxes, has been boosted in the polls by a campaign for an environmental bond issue, according to a survey released Tuesday.

The Quinnipiac College Poll found that Pataki's job approval rating among New York state voters was 56 to 34 percent compared with the 53 to 31 percent approval he received in an October 1996 poll conducted by the Hamden, Connecticut, college.
"Since the big gain he made by pushing last year's environmental bond issue, Gov. Pataki has been riding high," said Maurice Carroll, director of the Quinnipiac College Polling Institute.

"The Governor wins solid approval in every area except education -- a constant concern, and taxes -- an even more constant concern. And low approval on the tax issue should be of some concern for Gov. Pataki."

Pataki, a little-known state senator before the 1994 race, scored a surprise victory over three-term Gov. Mario Cuomo, a national figure in the Democratic Party. Pataki moved swiftly to restore the death penalty when he took office. Cuomo, who opposes capital punishment, consistently vetoed death penalty legislation passed by the state assembly.

The environmental bond issue approved by voters in 1996 was expected to raise money to help clean up industrial sites, toxic waste and sewage treatment plants and be used for other environmental improvements.
The poll surveyed 1,071 New Yorkers who say they are registered voters. The poll was conducted Feb. 24 to March 2 and has a margin of error of plus or minus three percent.

Republicans approve of the job Pataki is doing by 81 to 12 percent, Democrats give him a negative approval rating of 41 to 48 percent and 54 to 35 percent of independents said they approve of the way he is doing his job, the poll found.
